facts.text: m8g.24xlarge (primary) fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity in BOTH eu-west-1a and eu-west-1b, at night peak (about 20:00-02:00 UTC): the pool for this size is short at peak.

m8g.16xlarge (fallback) fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity only in eu-west-1a, only around 01:00-03:00 UTC, while the account team's snapshot shows 240 free m8g.16xlarge in eu-west-1a at those times. So pool depth does not explain it; the evidence should go to the AWS account team / TAM to investigate (e.g. account-level limits).

c8g.4xlarge fails with VcpuLimitExceeded in a different Auto Scaling group (batch-etl-asg): a real On-Demand vCPU quota problem, fixed via Service Quotas, unrelated to the Graviton web rollout's capacity.
m8g.16xlarge in eu-west-1b fails with InsufficientFreeAddressesInSubnet (subnet-0bbb2222): a subnet IP space problem, fixed by adding IP space/subnets.

Duplicates are removed before counting: the same record appearing twice (same eventID) and several rows for the same API request (same requestID). Counts are based on 1,161 unique requests out of 3,754 rows; 465 instances failed with capacity errors in total.
Recommends continuing the rollout (not pausing as the first answer), with concrete actions and an owner for each (customer platform team / AWS account team or TAM / customer for quota).

wrong_claims.text: Suggests a quota increase as the fix for InsufficientInstanceCapacity errors.
Treats the m8g.16xlarge eu-west-1a failures as a normal pool shortage, ignoring that the snapshot showed free capacity.
Recommends pausing or rolling back the Graviton rollout as the main answer.
Reports failure counts inflated by duplicate records (e.g. counts higher than 210 / 165 / 90 for the capacity errors).
Blames the c8g.4xlarge quota errors or the subnet errors on Graviton capacity.
